ANIMAL CATEGORIES LESSON · ANIMAL CATEGORIES · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Farm Birds — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the birds of the barnyard, one feather at a time.

What is this?

Farm birds are the feathered farm workers: chickens lay the eggs, ducks paddle and forage, turkeys strut, and geese act as the barnyard’s alarm system.

What does it mean?

Birds are not just farm extras — they are a whole crew with different jobs: breakfast, pest control, watchdog duties and feather-down pillows.

What does the child need to know?

Chickens lay eggs almost daily; ducks have waterproof feathers thanks to a special oil they spread from a spot near their tails; turkeys can change the color of their face skin; geese fly in V-formations and remember faces for years.

Why this matters

Eggs are probably the first food your child can trace to its source — the chicken did it, this morning, and the egg carton is the proof.

What it teaches

Sound discrimination (cluck, quack, gobble, honk), waddle-and-strut body play, and the first food-chain story: hen → egg → breakfast.

Words to learn

chickenheneggduckturkeygoosehonkfeatherbeaknest

Say this to your child

“"Farm birds run the morning! The hen lays the eggs, the duck paddles the pond, the turkey gobbles and struts, and the goose honks at anything new. Feathers up, everyone!"”

Step by step

  1. Start at the egg carton in the fridge: "who made these? The hen — almost one a day!"
  2. The duck: waterproof feathers and paddle feet — it can swim all day and stays dry. Quack.
  3. The turkey: the strutter — its tail fans out like a parade wheel and it gobbles loud enough to hear across the farm.
  4. The goose: the guard goose — honks at strangers, hisses at intruders, and many farms use geese instead of watchdogs.
  5. Walk them all: waddle like a duck, strut like a turkey, march like a goose on patrol, scratch like a chicken.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, the chicken pecks in front, the duck sits low and round, the turkey shows a full fan of tail feathers, and the goose stands tallest with its long neck — the lookout.

Ask your child

"Who gives us eggs?" (the hen) "Which bird swims?" (the duck) "Which bird is the farm’s alarm bell?" (the goose)

What your child can say or do

Your child might gobble at the dinner table in November, waddle to the bath announcing "duck!", or check the fridge carton and thank the hens personally.

Out in the real world

Thanksgiving in the US and Canada centers the turkey — children who know this card can explain the whole bird. Goose-fair season and duck-pond visits make the rest of the card real.

Try it together

Egg-and-spoon farm: carry a boiled egg on a spoon across the "barnyard" without dropping it — the hen’s delivery route. Add the honk: the goose patrol honks whenever a wobbly walker goes by.

Understanding check

Ask: "Which farm bird swims?" (the duck) "Which one lays the eggs we eat?" (the chicken) "Which bird honks like an alarm?" (the goose)

This lesson pairs with the Farm Birds flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Animal Categories.
